svg.title: CloudMart architecture diagram
svg.desc: Browser and React SPA reach Static Web Apps and the App Service API through Front Door. The API publishes to Service Bus and Event Hubs; Event Grid relays Blob events; Azure Functions process all three, and run the order saga that charges through the Payments API, books through the Shipping API and refunds on failure. Service Bus Standard has no private endpoints, so it is reached on its public endpoint with Entra ID; Event Grid pushes to the Function App's public endpoint. The APIs and Functions send outbound traffic through VNet-integrated subnets to private endpoints for Azure SQL, Cosmos DB, Key Vault, Event Hubs, Storage and the Payments and Shipping APIs. Each subnet has a network security group. Optionally (phase 13), a hub VNet with Azure Firewall Basic is peered to this spoke, and a route table sends the app subnets' internet-bound traffic through the firewall, which allows only Service Bus, Entra ID and Azure Monitor; private endpoint traffic stays direct. Telemetry and diagnostic logs flow to Application Insights and Log Analytics, where log search and metric alerts (exceptions, dead letters, backlog, throttling, orders needing review) notify an action group.
svg.text: CloudMart on Azure: request path, the order saga, network isolation and monitoring. It runs in memory on a laptop; each learning phase switches on more of what is shown here.

Subnets and NSGs keep the tiers apart. Add a
VNet per region or environment, not per app: the
microservices and Event Hubs use private endpoints
here. Shared services go in a hub (phase 13).
PE /32 routes are more specific: data goes direct.

svg.text: NSG: pe-nsg allows the VNet on TCP 443, 1433, 5432 and AMQP 5671-5672, denies the rest. Each name resolves to its endpoint through a private DNS zone.
